title: Lyra ensemble: deterministic preflight and quality gates for LTS rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an "Lyra ensemble" of deterministic preflight checks and quality gates to validate runtime-1.20 candidate images before promoting to LTS channels. The ensemble must run automatically as part of the release pipeline and produce a single pass/fail verdict with graded signals. The scope includes: 1) Lightweight startup + health smoke probes (API handshake, KV priming, streaming handshake); 2) Mini perf microbench (p50/p95/p99 token latency, throughput at target batch sizes) with deterministic synthetic traces; 3) Quality eval suite (curated 120-prompt set across production intents covering hallucination, answer stability, safety regressions) run on the candidate model configs; 4) Regression fingerprint comparison against the current LTS baseline using numeric thresholds and per-prompt diffs; 5) Integration with rollout orchestration to gate canary -> ramp based on pass/fail and soft degradations. Acceptance criteria: - Ensemble runs under 20 minutes for a candidate image in the CI pipeline; - Perf thresholds: p99 latency must not increase >15% vs LTS baseline and error rate <0.5%; - Eval quality: top-level quality score not decrease by more than 2 points and no single prompt regression with >10% degraded accuracy; - KV cache priming observed (cache hit rate >60%) on synthetic prefix scenarios; - Automated verdict emitted to rollouts service with attached artifacts (raw traces, diffs, metric summary) and dashboard link. Deliverables: test harness repo updates, CI orchestration changes, dashboard widgets, runbook for triage and manual override, and a canary gating policy document.
comments: 2025-11-12: Kickoff — scoped Lyra ensemble after spike showed that existing smoke + perf runs were taking >45m and lacked per-prompt quality checks. Decided to trade some breadth (full eval) for deterministic, targeted 120-prompt suite to keep latency under 20m.

2025-11-14: Design review with PM and Research — PM (Ravi Shah) requested explicit customer-impact mapping for each failure mode; Research suggested adding a small contextual diversity set to detect hallucination regressions. Action: add 20 'safety' probes to the suite, mark them high-weight.

2025-11-18: Engineering design — proposed harness layout: containerized runner that mounts candidate image, runs three phases (smoke, perf-micro, eval). Use existing perf harness but with deterministic seed traces; reuse KV priming script from ENG-509233 with small modifications. Added a 2-minute 'warmup' step to avoid transient cold-start noise.

2025-11-20: PM feedback — require explicit manual-override path in console and email pager rule only for 'hard-fail' verdicts. Also asked to export per-prompt diffs to GCS for downstream analysis. Added export step to pipeline.

2025-11-22: QA note — synthetic workload needs to emulate multi-tenant request headers to validate routing and tenant isolation; added tenant header permutations. Also identified flakiness on one safety prompt (TBD flaky prompt id=047); QA to triage and possibly remove if non-actionable.

2025-11-25: First infra run — Lyra completed in 18m (smoke 2m, perf 7m, eval 9m). Perf p99 increased 9% vs baseline, eval top-level score -0.8 points. Verdict: PASS (soft-degrade). Artifacts uploaded: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/release-lyra and gs://redwood-evals/lyra/2025-11-25/results.json. Logged PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4532

2025-11-26: Security review kickoff — security requested proof of deterministic seed sources and that the eval runner does not exfiltrate prompts. Added encryption-at-rest for GCS artifacts and reviewed runner perms. Security checklist updated in Confluence.

2025-11-27: Risk & rollout planning — SRE raised concern about running the ensemble against heavy GPU-backed images in the shared staging cluster. Decision: schedule Lyra runs on isolated preflight pool (dedicated test GPUs) to avoid noisy neighbor interference. SRE to provision pool (ticket: ENG-881900).
2025-11-28: Ready for full CI integration — created draft pipeline job and staging dashboard. Next: finalize canary gating logic and author rollout policy doc for release engineers.
